title: Developer Toolbelt: Quickstart scripts & onboarding sketch
content:
Overview:

This is a lightweight sketch for a developer-facing "toolbelt" quickstart: a set of short scripts, a tiny CLI wrapper, and a one-page checklist that lets engineers on any platform get a minimal Redwood SDK-based integration up and running in under 8 minutes. The goal is not to replace the full quickstart guides but to provide a practical, copy-paste friendly path that covers the most common first-week tasks for product engineers: generate, chat, and embed.

Audience:
- Product engineers and backend engineers who want a fast PoC path
- Solutions engineers doing demos for customers
- Oncall engineers who need repro scripts for troubleshooting

Constraints & principles:
- Must be runnable in a local dev environment (macOS/Linux/WSL) without cloud creds beyond an API key
- Single-file examples preferred (script or tiny app)
- Minimal dependencies; prefer the official Redwood SDK only
- Include simple network failure handling and a fallback sample (local toy model stub)
- Instrument basic telemetry events for onboarding funnel analysis

Quickstart flows (three compact paths):
1) Minimal CLI generation (bash one-liner + node/python wrapper)
2) Chat endpoint demo (serverless example using express/fastify)
3) Embeddings + vector search (python script to index small README and run similarity)

Example: Bash one-liner (user story: "I want to generate a commit message for changed files"):
- copy/paste:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize changed files into a concise commit message: added tests, fixed bug in auth"}' | jq -r '.output[0].content'

Notes: include a tiny cross-platform jq fallback or print raw JSON if jq missing. Add a --stream flag example for streaming.

Example: Tiny Python embedding + search (copyable)
- goals: show embeddings, simple local cosine search, show token usage
- snippet (pseudo):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  docs = ["README: install steps...","Changelog: v1.2 fixes X"]
  emb = client.embeddings.create(model='emb-small', input=docs)
  # store vector list, run cosine similarity against query

UX and telemetry hooks (lightweight):
- emit events: quickstart.started, quickstart.completed, sample-run.failed (include reason code)
- attach minimal context: os, runtime (node/python), sample_path, duration_ms
- backend: ensure events surface in devexp analytics dashboard (Confluence ticket linked)

CLI wrapper idea: "rdw" small binary written in node that:
- scaffolds a project folder with templates (server, embed, generate)
- validates REDWOOD_API_KEY presence and suggests how to set it locally
- runs smoke tests: a single request per template to validate connectivity
- prints cost estimate (rough) based on token usage from response

Error handling examples to include in docs:
- network timeout -> retry once after 250ms, then show guidance about region mismatch
- 401/403 -> clear error message pointing to billing/keys page and to support link
- 429 -> show polite backoff suggestion and link to docs for rate limits and Dedicated plans

Security & compliance note:
- quickstarts must avoid embedding secrets in checked-in files. Template .env.sample and a pre-commit hook snippet recommended.
- add one small section explaining how to use KMS-backed secrets for Private/Dedicated customers (high level).

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal) — circulate these scripts to SEs and two product teams for feedback (2 weeks)
- Phase 1 (beta) — ship as part of SDK 0.9 release, include telemetry opt-in, sample usage metrics (4 weeks)
- Phase 2 (public) — polish docs, record short 90s screencast, PR to docs site and quickstart landing (2 weeks)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should the rdw CLI auto-create a free sandbox key or open a prefilled signup page? (privacy/legal question)
- Where to store telemetry flags for opt-out? (account-level vs local)
- Can we include a tiny wasm fallback model for airgapped demos? feasibility ticket needed.

Checklist for a single quickstart template (for authoring):
- [ ] single-file example present (bash/node/python)
- [ ] copy/paste runnable in under 8 minutes
- [ ] telemetry events instrumented and documented
- [ ] clear failure messages for common errors (401, 429, timeout)
- [ ] .env.sample and README tutorial steps
- [ ] link to full API docs and SDK reference

Notes to self / stray ideas (informal):
- Add a short "Why Redwood" blurb at top focused on latency/cost toggles — helps SEs during demos
- Consider a "debug mode" env var that prints request headers and token counts for training new SEs
- Maybe a tiny browser-based sandbox (static page) that uses a short-lived token via Redirect flow — follow up with security team

References & related work:
- See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 for earlier bootstrap code
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-DEVEXP-178 (onboarding telemetry)
- Slack thread: #devexp-onboarding (msg12345) contains user feedback from SEs re: friction on Windows

Next steps (actionable):
1) Sync with Marco and Priya to pick canonical 3 templates by EOD Friday.
2) Create rdw node repo skeleton and small acceptance tests (assign Samir).
3) Draft one-page quickstart landing copy for docs site and record a 90s demo video (owner: Elena).

-- end of sketch --

This doc is intentionally terse and pragmatic. It's a working doc: feel free to paste TODOs into the linked PR or open follow-up tickets in the devexp board.
